**Notch mode, and the first macOS build.**

## Notch mode

On a MacBook with a camera housing, the widget can put itself away and grow the notch
instead. The housing reaches a little further down the screen and the 5-hour session runs
along the bottom of it — the same twenty ticks and the same redline as the full bar, with
nothing around them. No label, no percentage, no countdown.

At 100% the meter changes what it measures. A full bar that stays full says nothing for
the hours it stays that way, so once the allowance is spent it switches to the wait for
the next one and fills again as the reset comes up, reaching full exactly when the session
returns. A lighter red marks the change of subject.

Turn it on in **Settings → Look**, or from the menu bar icon. The switch stays hidden on a
Mac without a notch.

## macOS builds

A `.dmg` ships for the first time — `-arm64` for Apple silicon, the plain one for Intel.

The build is **ad-hoc signed**: there is no Apple Developer ID behind this project, so
macOS refuses the first launch of a copy that came from the internet, usually with
*"Claude Usage is damaged and can't be opened"*. It is not damaged — that is the quarantine
flag, and clearing it is one command:

```bash
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Claude Usage.app"
```

Once per download, not once per launch.

That command opts this app out of the check macOS does on unidentified binaries, so it is
worth knowing what you are trusting. Every installer below is built by a GitHub runner from
the tagged commit rather than uploaded from anyone's machine — the build log is public, and
the SHA-256 of each file is at the bottom of these notes to check a download against.

The same missing signature means a Mac copy cannot replace itself in place, so new versions
come from this page. Windows updates itself as before.
